content.text: Add view transitions to this product gallery app. When navigating from the grid to a product detail page, the product image should smoothly morph between the thumbnail and the large detail image using a shared element transition. Page navigations should slide directionally. Suspense loading states should transition smoothly from skeleton to content. All animations must respect the user's prefers-reduced-motion preference.
I'll explore the product gallery app structure first to see how routing, images, and loading states are set up.

React's `<ViewTransition>` component integrates with the browser's [View Transitions API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/View_Transition_API) to handle this declaratively. You name the elements that should persist, and the browser animates between their old and new positions.

View transitions work in the App Router with no configuration. The App Router uses [React canary releases](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries), which contain all stable React 19 changes as well as newer features like `ViewTransition`. You do not need to install `react@canary` yourself.

`<ViewTransition>` animations are activated by [Transitions](https://react.dev/reference/react/useTransition), [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense), and [`useDeferredValue`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useDeferredValue). Regular `setState` calls do not trigger them. In Next.js, route navigations are transitions, so `<ViewTransition>` animations activate automatically during navigation.

content.text:
View transitions are wired up across the gallery. Here's what changed:

### Shared element morph (grid → detail)
Product thumbnails and hero images share a `ViewTransition` name (`product-{slug}`) with `share="morph"`, so the colored image block morphs from the grid card into the detail hero.

### Directional page navigation
- Grid links use `transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}` — new page slides in from the right
- Back link uses `transitionTypes={['nav-back']}` — grid slides back in from the left
- Both pages wrap content in `ViewTransition` with matching `enter`/`exit` mappings

### Suspense skeleton → content
Skeleton fallbacks use `exit="slide-down"` and loaded content uses `enter="slide-up"`, with staggered fade/slide timing so the handoff feels smooth rather than abrupt.

### Reduced motion
A `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` block disables all view-transition animations and skeleton pulse effects, so content swaps instantly for users who prefer less motion.

### CSS additions (`globals.css`)
Timing variables, fade/slide keyframes, directional nav rules, morph blur, and `pointer-events: none` on `::view-transition` so the page stays interactive during transitions.

`ProductGrid` now suspends briefly (like `ProductDetails`) so the home page skeleton transition is visible on load. The build completes successfully.

View transitions are wired up across the gallery. Here's what changed:

### Shared element morph (grid → detail)
Product thumbnails and hero images share a `ViewTransition` name (`product-{slug}`) with `share="morph"`, so the colored image block morphs from the grid card into the detail hero.

### Directional page navigation
- Grid links use `transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}` — new page slides in from the right
- Back link uses `transitionTypes={['nav-back']}` — grid slides back in from the left
- Both pages wrap content in `ViewTransition` with matching `enter`/`exit` mappings

### Suspense skeleton → content
Skeleton fallbacks use `exit="slide-down"` and loaded content uses `enter="slide-up"`, with staggered fade/slide timing so the handoff feels smooth rather than abrupt.

### Reduced motion
A `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` block disables all view-transition animations and skeleton pulse effects, so content swaps instantly for users who prefer less motion.

### CSS additions (`globals.css`)
Timing variables, fade/slide keyframes, directional nav rules, morph blur, and `pointer-events: none` on `::view-transition` so the page stays interactive during transitions.

`ProductGrid` now suspends briefly (like `ProductDetails`) so the home page skeleton transition is visible on load. The build completes successfully.
